issues.legal_issue: A first appellate court must independently consider the evidence and decide the issues raised by the parties through a reasoned judgment.
material_facts: The appellant brought first appeals from a trial court decree dismissing one suit and decreeing a related suit.
The High Court dismissed both appeals cursorily without appreciating the evidence, addressing the issues, or discussing the parties’ arguments.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court set aside the High Court’s judgment and remanded both first appeals for fresh decision on the merits in accordance with law, without expressing any view on the merits of the dispute.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 96 read with Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, a first appeal is a valuable right and, unless restricted by law, opens the case for rehearing on fact and law. The first appellate court must consider the evidence, address all issues and contentions pressed by the parties, and give reasons for its findings; if reversing a factual finding, it must engage with the trial court’s reasoning and explain its own. The Court relied on Kurian Chacko v. Varkey Ouseph, AIR 1969 Kerala 316; Santosh Hazari v. Purushottam Tiwari, (2001) 3 SCC 179; Madhukar v. Sangram, (2001) 4 SCC 756; H.K.N. Swami v. Irshad Basith, (2005) 10 SCC 243; Jagannath v. Arulappa, (2005) 12 SCC 303; B.V. Nagesh v. H.V. Sreenivasa Murthy, (2010) 13 SCC 530; State Bank of India v. Emmsons International Ltd., (2011) 12 SCC 174; and Union of India v. K.V. Lakshman, (2016) 13 SCC 124.

predicates.first_appeal_from_original_decree: A party brought a first appeal from a decree made by a trial court.
predicates.appellate_court_omitted_evidence_review: The appellate court failed to consider and appraise the evidence relevant to the appeal.
predicates.appellate_court_omitted_reasoned_issue_f: The appellate court failed to address the issues or contentions requiring decision and give reasons for its findings.
predicates.appeal_remanded_for_fresh_reasoned_decis: The appeal is sent back for a fresh decision that addresses the issues and evidence with reasons.

issues.definition: When a first appeal from a trial decree is decided without evidence review or reasoned findings on the issues, the appeal is sent back for a fresh reasoned decision.
